items.title: Police hunt woman who kicked auxiliary policeman in groin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are tracking down a woman who kicked an auxiliary policeman in the groin after he confronted her for driving against traffic flow near a shopping complex in Damansara yesterday. Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said the incident occurred at 8.38am while the 30-year-old auxiliary policeman was on duty. "However, the suspect showed an obscene gesture," Hoo said when contacted.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Thursday, Oct 15, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1556387]] [[nid:1556386]] [[nid:1556385]] [[nid:1556384]] [[nid:1556383]] [[nid:1556382]] [[nid:1556381]] [[nid:1556380]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Malaysians in Istanbul safe amid flash floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: No Malaysians are affected by floods in Istanbul, Turkiye, following unusually heavy rain and strong winds since late Tuesday night. Malaysian Consul in Istanbul Mardhiah Sabri said the consulate was closely monitoring the situation to ensure Malaysians' safety in the city. She said heavy rain since Oct 13 had flooded several parts of Istanbul, affecting roads and residential areas.

items.title: Haze forces postponement of UASA next week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry has postponed the Academic Year-End Assessment (UASA), scheduled for next week, due to the haze affecting the country. In a statement today, the ministry said the decision was made after taking into account concerns raised by parents and guardians over their children's health, particularly those who would need to attend school to sit for the assessment. The ministry acknowledged the dilemma faced by parents who wanted to protect their children's health but were also concerned that their absence from school could result in them missing an important assessment.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 15, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: BYD driver charged The driver involved in a six-vehicle crash that killed a five-year-old girl has claimed trial to three traffic offences and was granted RM36,000 bail. Classmate charged with murder A 16-year-old student has been charged with murdering classmate Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal at a school in Yong Peng. Shaik faces 15 charges Government agency chairman Datuk Dr Shaik Hussein Mydin has claimed trial to 15 corruption charges involving RM847,107 in alleged bribes linked to a hostel project.

items.title: PM Anwar vows to fast‑track UM hostel project, says no leakages or wastage allowed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the Universiti Malaya (UM) Student Residence project to serve as a model for development management that is clean, efficient, and free from leakages or the wastage of public funds. He said the implementation of this project must draw lessons from the shortcomings of past project management which led to cost overruns, delays, and abandoned construction sites ultimately resulting in losses for the nation. Therefore, vice-chancellor, ensure that UM and this Student Residence project become an example for other agencies to emulate.

items.title: Ministry studies OTP to curb abandoned projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry is studying a proposed option-to-purchase (OTP) mechanism to reduce sick and abandoned housing projects and better protect homebuyers. Its minister Nga Kor Ming said the mechanism would introduce a more structured process before sale and purchase agreements are signed, allowing developers to gauge genuine demand while safeguarding buyers' interests. "At present, developers often assess market demand through the collection of booking fees.

items.title: MOE reverts to haze plan: Schools shut at API 200, outdoor classes at 100, parents may keep kids home
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has reverted to the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK) guidelines, which mandate the immediate closure of schools when the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaches 200, following input from various relevant agencies. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said that under the PTJK, all outdoor classroom activities must also be halted when the API exceeds 100. “In managing the haze, specific actions must be taken for each API reading level.

items.title: Private hospitals expect faster licensing with e-CKAPS portal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Private hospitals expect less paperwork, shorter approval times and greater certainty for operators with the introduction of a fully digitalised licensing system under the 2027 Budget. Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh said the e-CKAPS portal would streamline the licensing process for private healthcare facilities, which has traditionally relied on manual procedures. "Licensing is one of the most process heavy areas for private hospitals, and our licensing process has been a manual process.

items.title: Another brazen cable theft caught on video, cops hunt 5 men in Johor
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police are hunting five men caught on video stealing cables in Taman Melodies here, after the footage went viral on social media. Johor Baru (South) police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said the video showed the men cutting cables and loading them into a car. He said an internal police report was lodged at 4.16pm yesterday after a senior police officer came across a social media post uploaded at 2.20pm the same day.

items.title: Conference of Rulers deliberates PM term limits, AG‑PP separation and Child Act amendments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The proposed constitutional amendments to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure and separate the roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor were among the key matters discussed at the 273rd Conference of Rulers meeting at Istana Negara. The two-day meeting, which began yesterday, was chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah. His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the second day’s proceedings, accompanied by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

items.title: CelcomDigi pays RM382mil for spectrum bands
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CelcomDigi Bhd has paid RM381.75 million for spectrum assignments in the 2600MHz and 900MHz frequency bands to strengthen network capacity and coverage. "The assignment enables a contiguous 2x40MHz spectrum holding in the 2600MHz spectrum frequency band and improves the company's spectrum position in the 900MHz spectrum frequency band to support wider and deeper coverage across the country," it said in a statement. The additional 2600MHz spectrum will expand CelcomDigi's contiguous spectrum holding in the band, while the 900MHz allocation is expected to strengthen coverage across the country.

items.title: GWM adds two outlets as deliveries rise
items.summary: GWM Skudai, operated by Auto Elegance Sdn Bhd, officially opened on Oct 8. The 22,006 sq ft facility combines sales, service and spare parts operations, with three service bays and capacity to service about 150 vehicles a month. It also has five vehicle display spaces, an electric vehicle charging station, diagnostic equipment and a dedicated vehicle delivery bay.

items.title: Haze: Schools in eight Selangor districts to close tomorrow
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Schools in eight districts in Selangor will be closed tomorrow due to the haze. The Selangor Education Department said the closure would affect schools under the Klang, Kuala Selangor, Kuala Langat, Hulu Langat, Gombak, Sepang, Petaling Perdana and Petaling Utama district education offices. Schools under the Hulu Selangor and Sabak Bernam district education offices will operate as usual.

items.title: Malaysian arrested in Singapore with more than 700 cigarette cartons hidden in car panels
items.summary: They uncovered more than 700 cartons and 2,000 packets of duty-unpaid cigarettes. Despite Singapore's tough stance on contraband, cigarette smuggling attempts persist, driven by the lucrative black market. The seizure highlights persistent cigarette smuggling attempts despite Singapore's tough stance on contraband, with high tobacco taxes creating a lucrative market for illicit cigarettes.

items.title: M'sian man held at Kualanamu Airport with syabu hidden in folded banknotes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 39-year-old man from Negri Sembilan was arrested by Indonesian Customs officers after arriving at Kualanamu International Airport in North Sumatra at 8am today. The suspect arrived on an AirAsia flight from Kuala Lumpur, according to Indonesian news portal Analisadaily.com. An unidentified Kualanamu Customs officer said the man was detained after authorities became suspicious during routine checks on his person and belongings at the international arrivals terminal.

items.title: Selangor schools in Klang, Petaling, Gombak and more closed tomorrow as haze worsens
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 15 — Schools under the Klang, Kuala Selangor, Kuala Langat, Hulu Langat, Gombak, Sepang, Petaling Perdana and Petaling Utama district education offices will be closed tomorrow due to the haze. However, the Selangor State Education Department (JPNS) said in a statement today that schools under the Hulu Selangor and Sabak Bernam district education offices will operate as usual. “Parents, guardians, students and the wider education community are advised to take note of this announcement and refer to JPNS channels for the latest updates,” the statement said.

items.title: Malaysia has no plans for legal action or diplomatic note to Indonesia over haze
items.summary: REMBAU: Malaysia has no plans to send a diplomatic note or take legal action against Indonesia over the transboundary haze currently affecting the country, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. "We have not reached that stage (of sending a diplomatic note). Mohamad, who is also Rembau MP, said sending a diplomatic note was not the best way forward, as Malaysia had to take its relationship with Indonesia into account.

items.title: Genting Plantations, Huawei team up on 174ha Johor tech campus
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Plantations Bhd's property arm has partnered with Huawei Technologies (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd to masterplan a 174-hectare smart campus in Johor, marking the Chinese technology group's first international smart campus partnership. Genting Property Sdn Bhd signed a master planning agreement with Huawei to advance the Johor Tech Smart City (JTSC) development, including its flagship Smart Campus within the Knowledge AI Campus. The partnership will bring Huawei's artificial intelligence capabilities, technological expertise and smart campus experience into the development's planning phase, drawing on its existing smart campus projects in Shanghai and Dongguan.

items.title: Bollywood actor Imran Khan asked to leave India after participating in protest
items.summary: MUMBAI: Indian authorities have asked Bollywood actor Imran Khan to leave the country by the end of the month, saying he breached immigration laws after joining a protest against the election commission chief, local media reported on Thursday. Khan, 43, is a US citizen, the Indian Express newspaper reported. — REUTERS © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: 'Anwar Ibrahim: A Life Recorded' book to be launched in March
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A book titled Anwar Ibrahim: A Life Recorded (Anwar Ibrahim: Kisah yang Dirakam), chronicling the life, struggles and leadership journey of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, will be launched in March next year. Published by the Malaysian Care and Concern for Humanity Organisation (Malaysia Peduli) in Bahasa Melayu and English, the book features photographs, archival materials, documents and historical records relating to the Prime Minister. Speaking to reporters, Muhammad Kamil said the book was important in helping younger generations understand the Prime Minister's life journey.

items.title: Activist, 2 others nabbed over temple statue vandalism
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Three people, including an activist, were remanded for three days to assist in investigations into the vandalism of four statues at a temple in Jalan Klang Lama on Oct 6. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the trio were arrested in Beranang, Selangor, on Oct 11 and released on police bail on Tuesday. "Initial investigations found that four religious statues at the temple had been damaged.

items.title: Sudden death probe opened after student’s fatal fall at Penang dormitory
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 15 — A female university student died after allegedly falling from a building in the hostel block of a higher education institute in Jalan Bukit Gambir, Gelugor here today. Timur Laut district police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the police received a phone call from the university at 8.40am informing them of the discovery of the body of a 21-year-old female student residing in the dormitory. The student’s body was found at 7.25am by the university’s cleaning staff.

items.title: Court upholds 30-year sentence for man who killed stepbrother, concealed body
items.summary: A three-judge panel comprising Judges Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar unanimously dismissed Mohamad Zamhuri Azami's appeal against his conviction and sentence. The panel also dismissed the prosecution's appeal to impose the death penalty on the 31-year-old accused. Delivering the court's unanimous decision, Noorin said the sentence imposed by the High Court was appropriate and did not warrant appellate intervention.

items.title: When accident is off-duty but the financial pain isn't [WATCH]
items.summary: FOR most workers, a workplace accident is easy enough to picture: a fall at a construction site, an injury involving machinery, a collision while making a delivery. In its first three months, PERKESO recorded 6,330 claims under the scheme, with RM9.97 million in benefits paid out. Other claims involved road accidents and incidents during workers' personal time.

items.title: Penang statutory body chief pleads not guilty to 15 graft charges totalling RM800,000
items.summary: Datuk Dr Shaik Hussein Mydin, 53, is accused of corruptly receiving RM847,107.61 through Aliran Ilham Sdn Bhd (AISB) in multiple transactions from ATSH Management Sdn Bhd (ATSH) director Datuk R. Albert Suresh. Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy public prosecutors Lim Jin Hong and Nurnajihatul Idayu Mohd Azuyar proposed bail of RM1 million, with additional conditions requiring the accused to surrender his passport, report to the MACC office monthly and refrain from interfering with prosecution witnesses. Shaik Hussein was represented by a seven-member legal team led by Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, comprising Datuk Hasnal Rezua Merican, Mohd Shahrullah Khan, Simon Tan, Dr Shamsher Singh Thind, Muzzammil Merican and Intan Nur Alia Nodzri.

items.title: Ancom Nylex's Q1 profit jumps 15pct to RM24.13mil on higher RM533.42mil revenue
items.summary: Revenue for the quarter under review climbed to RM533.42 million from RM447.36 million a year ago. Its industrial chemicals segment saw selling prices move higher alongside firmer crude oil prices. The segment's revenue climbed 32.8 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM355.9 million from RM268 million previously, while pre-tax earnings almost doubled to RM19.4 million from RM10.2 million.

items.title: 6,363 citizenship applications still under consideration, says Home Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 6,363 citizenship applications remained under consideration as of Sept 30, following 16,338 applications received between Jan 1, 2024 and Sept 30 this year. Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said 4,583 applications had been approved, with citizenship certificates issued. On applications through naturalisation, he said the provision under Article 19(1) of the Federal Constitution applied to certain categories of adults born overseas to Malaysian mothers.

items.title: Court of Appeal upholds 30‑year jail, 12 strokes for trader who hid step‑brother’s body in cement drum
items.summary: A three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar unanimously dismissed Mohamad Zamhuri Azami’s appeal against his conviction and sentence. The panel also dismissed the prosecution’s appeal to impose the death penalty on the 31-year-old accused. Delivering the court’s unanimous decision, Justice Noorin said the sentence imposed by the High Court was appropriate and did not warrant appellate intervention.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 15, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock index closed in the red as the post-budget rally lost momentum, amid renewed weakness in global technology stocks. The key index dropped four points to close at 1,623 on Thursday. In the crypto exchange, Bitcoin slipped to RM331,392.

items.title: Malaysia’s haze map turns red: Klang, Nilai, Shah Alam among worst affected at near‑200 API
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A total of 34 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today, with Klang, Selangor recording the highest reading at 195. A total of 34 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while no areas recorded good air quality. API readings between zero and 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 indicate moderate air quality, 101 to 200 indicate unhealthy air quality, 201 to 300 indicate very unhealthy air quality, while readings above 300 are classified as hazardous.

items.title: Vestland bags RM225mil Kelantan river project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Vestland Bhd, through its indirect wholly-owned Vestland Infra Sdn Bhd, has secured a RM225.07 million contract for river widening and related works under the Integrated River Basin Development project in Kelantan. Pembinaan Rizen Sdn Bhd awarded the contract, and Vestland Infra accepted the letter of award on Oct 15. The scope covers river widening, structural and associated works.

items.title: Astaka Padu and Kimlun in RM450mil Amora serviced residence project in Johor Bahru
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Astaka Padu Sdn Bhd and Kimlun Corporation Bhd have announced their latest joint development, the RM450 million gross development value Amora serviced residence. This project represents the fourth collaboration between the two Johor-based groups and will be executed through their joint venture company, Astaka Kimlun Sdn Bhd. Located on 2.45 acres of freehold commercial land in Tampoi, Johor Bahru, Amora serviced residence sits adjacent to the Pasir Gudang Highway and a 15-acre urban park.

items.title: 14, including two minors, charged with murder of 19-year-old youth in Gurun
items.summary: The accused are Muhammad Asyraaf Muhammad Zaidi, 20; Muhammad Azrul Rahimi Muhamad Yusri, 18; Ahmad Izzul Irfan Ridduan, 21; Muhammad Rhahimy Abdul Rashid, 19; Yusman Hakimi Yusmezal, 24; Muhammad Zulfaqar Zulkarnain Khairol Fais, 21; and Muhammad Aiman Riduwan Abdullah, 21. The other accused are Ahmad Aiman Danial Ahmad Wizam, 21; Muhammad Adam Haris Rosdan, 21; Muhammad Muqkriz Azizan, 21; Muhammad Adam Iqbal Mohd Wazir, 19; Syafiq Afif Syarafuddin Abd Ghapar, 23; and two minors aged 16 and 17. They were jointly charged with murdering Muhammad Haikal Mohd Shahrilnizam, 19, at an unnumbered house in Jalan Sungai Petani here, between 9pm on Oct 5 and 7.30am on Oct 8.

items.title: Next-of-kin of Long Lellang crash victims to receive RM130,000 in benefits, monthly pensions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The next-of-kin of four Health Ministry (MoH) staff who perished in a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak, will receive at least RM130,000 each in lump-sum benefits. MoH said the payments, which were being coordinated with the Public Service Department (PSD) and Sarawak Health Department, comprised several benefits including payment for unutilised leave, derivative gratuity, funeral management assistance and the Death Ex-Gratia payment. The ministry said eligible dependents would also begin receiving monthly derivative pensions from Oct 21, with payments distributed according to each beneficiary's entitlement under existing legal provisions.

items.title: Dzulkefly: Families of MOH staff killed in Sarawak helicopter crash to receive pensions from Oct 21
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 15 — The next-of-kin of four Ministry of Health (MOH) staff who perished in a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak, will begin receiving monthly derivative pension payments starting Oct 21. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said MOH, in collaboration with the Public Service Department (PSD) and the Sarawak State Health Department, has managed the disbursement of derivative pension benefits and appropriate financial assistance to the next-of-kin in a comprehensive and prudent manner. He noted that the total lump-sum payments for which the next-of-kin are eligible include compensation for accumulated leave (GCR), a derivative gratuity, funeral expense assistance, and an ex-gratia death payment.

items.title: UM student residence project to house 10,000 students by 2030
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Malaya's (UM) first phase of its student residence project is scheduled for completion in 2030, providing accommodation for 10,000 students amid concerns over university housing shortages. UM vice-chancellor Professor Datuk Seri Dr Noor Azuan Abu Osman said the project, to be developed on a 4.17-hectare site at the university's Fifth Residential College, marked a significant step towards meeting students' accommodation needs. Noor Azuan said he hoped the government would expedite the project, warning that students could graduate before its first block was built if implementation was delayed.

items.title: E-Commerce Bill crucial for healthy digital economy, fair competition - MRCA
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The E-Commerce Bill is a crucial step toward fostering a healthy digital economy, protecting consumer interests, and upholding fair market competition, said the Malaysia Retail Chain Association (MRCA). MRCA president Datuk Liew Bin emphasised that all businesses operating in Malaysia, domestic or foreign, must strictly adhere to statutory requirements regarding taxation, product safety, consumer protection, and commercial compliance. Concurrently, MRCA said the government should scale up digital adoption support for domestic SMEs, helping them develop omnichannel capabilities, strengthen brand equity, and tap overseas markets.

items.title: Rulers discuss bills on PM's tenure limit, separation of A-G and public prosecutor roles
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Conference of Rulers has discussed proposed constitutional amendments to limit the prime minister's tenure and separate the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor at its 273rd meeting. The meeting was chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah. All Rulers and state governors attended the first day of the meeting including the Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, Crown Prince of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra and Tunku Temenggong of Johor, Tunku Idris Iskandar Sultan Ibrahim.

items.title: KL police chief: Chemistry, pathology reports pending in custodial death case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Police are awaiting the full report from the Chemistry Department and official pathology results to complete their investigation into the recent death of a man in police custody. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the cause of death of the local man, who was in his 40s, had yet to be determined pending the reports. He said the investigation was being conducted independently and thoroughly by the Bukit Aman Death in Custody Criminal Investigation Unit (USJKT), in collaboration with the Integrity and Standards Compliance Department (JIPS).

items.title: Woman brushing teeth behind wheel flashes middle finger before kicking auxiliary cop in groin at Glo Damansara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A woman who was allegedly brushing her teeth behind the wheel flashed her middle finger at an auxiliary police officer before getting out of her car and kicking him in the groin during a bizarre confrontation at Glo Damansara yesterday. The woman then managed to escape after a struggle with the 30-year-old officer, leaving police hunting for her following the incident in Taman Tun Dr Ismail (TTDI). Brickfields district police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the officer approached the car to reprimand the woman and instruct her to move her vehicle.

items.title: Selangor, Putrajaya, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang schools stay open tomorrow amid haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — All educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Negeri Sembilan, Pahang, Selangor, and Putrajaya will operate as usual tomorrow. In separate statements today, the State Education Departments (JPN) in the three states and the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department (JPWPP) encouraged all pupils, teachers, support staff (AKP), and school personnel to wear face masks. In Negeri Sembilan, the JPN said all outdoor activities — including physical education, co-curricular and sports activities, camps, celebrations, assemblies, and open-hall events — must cease if the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 100.

items.title: Honeymoon hiccup: Malaysian couple’s car triggers Bangkok bomb scare
items.summary: BANGKOK, Oct 15 — A Malaysian couple on their honeymoon in Thailand sparked a security alert in Bangkok on Wednesday after their car was found parked in a prohibited area, prompting authorities to call in an Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) team to inspect the vehicle. Metropolitan Police Bureau Commissioner Pol Lt Gen Siam Boonsom said the Malaysian-registered red car was found parked on the pavement along Sukhumvit 17 Lane in Bangkok’s Lumpini district, raising concerns amid heightened security for the ongoing IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings 2026. He said Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) officials spotted the vehicle during a patrol on Wednesday afternoon and alerted the authorities over concerns that it might contain hazardous materials.

items.title: Selangor launches SA500 financing scheme for SMEs, NINE super app to consolidate services
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Selangor today launched a financing initiative for businesses facing cash flow constraints alongside a super app intended to bring government services, payments and mobility options onto a single digital platform. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said Selangor Advance 500 (SA500) would help eligible companies and contractors undertaking state-related projects manage their cash flow, while the NINE Super App would make government services and everyday transactions more accessible to the public. Amirudin said access to financing remained a challenge for many businesses, with SA500 intended to ease cash flow pressures and help eligible companies sustain their operations.

items.title: Seven seats in play, 21 firmly held: Zahid stakes out BN’s position in Melaka
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has said it will retain the 21 seats it won in the previous Melaka state election, leaving Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) component parties to negotiate over the remaining seven constituencies as discussions over electoral cooperation continue ahead of next month’s polls. BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition was holding talks with PN’s core parties following the suspension of activities by the Opposition coalition, but made clear that BN had no intention of giving up the seats it currently holds. He said statements by PH leaders at both national and state levels indicated that the coalition had lost interest in working with BN for the Melaka election.

items.title: Pushing mega-projects, Hamzah Zainudin criticises Budget 2027 as ‘lacking vision’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today criticised Budget 2027 as “lacking vision”, arguing that the federal government’s spending plan lacks a long-term economic plan and relies heavily on short-term handouts. Hamzah (PN-Larut) cited the government’s failure to meet its target of RM90 billion in development expenditure for two consecutive years, arguing this indicates poor fiscal management that could fuel concerns about potential under-investment in infrastructure projects. Anwar tabled a record RM459 billion federal spending plan for next year, of which some RM83 billion is earmarked for development.

items.title: Veterinary extension officers key to Malaysia’s food security, says deputy minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 15 — Veterinary extension officers play a crucial role in bridging government policies, the expertise of the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and the farming community to boost livestock productivity and strengthen national food security. Themed “Veterinary Extension: A Driver for Productivity and Food Security”, the convention was also attended by Veterinary Services Department director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Noor Hisham Mohd Haron. The categories included Best State Veterinary Service, Best District Veterinary Service, Best Livestock-Based Industry Development Project, Best Veterinary Extension Project, Best Veterinary Extension Project Poster, Best Veterinary Extension Project Video Presentation, Best Veterinary Extension Mentor/Officer and Best VetEC (Veterinary Extension Centre) Operation.

items.title: Budget 2027: RM130M boost for local film, music, and creative content
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The allocation of more than RM130 million under Budget 2027 for the local film, music and creative industries is a timely move to boost the sector’s contribution to economic growth and talent development. MyCreative Ventures said in a statement today that the government’s support would help industry players nurture their talents, create high-quality content and build more resilient and sustainable creative businesses. “In an industry increasingly shaped by technology, digital content and global competition, creativity must extend beyond producing works to generating greater economic value,” it said.

items.title: Kepong knife attack: Chinese student charged with stabbing ex-girlfriend and her brother
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A 20-year-old Chinese national university student pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to two charges of causing grievous hurt by stabbing his former girlfriend and her younger brother with a knife last month. Chen Jun is accused of causing grievous hurt to Leong Kai Ting, 21, and her younger brother, Leong Shun Jie, 18, by stabbing them both with a knife capable of causing death. Chen Jun appeared in court in a wheelchair.

items.title: Perikatan ‘almost 100pc’ certain of Melaka election alliance, but Takiyuddin keeps potential partners under wraps
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is almost certain to forge an alliance with other political parties ahead of the Melaka state election, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today, although he stopped short of revealing who its potential partners might be. Takiyuddin did not disclose which parties PN was negotiating with or whether the talks involved BN. He said discussions over seat allocations were already under way, both with potential allies and among PN’s own component parties.

items.title: Zetrix AI pledges cooperation as police, MACC probe unpaid RM314m collections
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Zetrix AI Bhd will fully cooperate with authorities in an ongoing joint investigation by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). The company was responding to a query from Bursa Malaysia Securities dated Oct 14 regarding a media report entitled "Police say six witnesses questioned in probe into MyEG, Zetrix AI” published by The Edge Malaysia on Oct 13. Zetrix AI said it would communicate any material developments through official announcements.

items.title: Court hears charges against former UKM director accused of RM3.12m contract abuse
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 15 — A former director of an education centre at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to two charges of abusing his position to secure employment contracts worth RM3.12 million in 2022. Datuk Prof Muhammad Hussin, 64, a retiree, entered the plea after the charges were read out before Judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin. According to the charges, Muhammad, a member of Koperasi Siswazah Bangi Berhad (KSBB), allegedly abused his position to secure two contracts worth RM1.2 million and RM1.92 million respectively to manage the Master of Education programme through UKM’s Faculty of Education.

items.title: Sarawak man finds RM1b in bank account, asks ChatGPT to count the zeros — only to discover it’s a glitch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — When a Sarawak clinic manager opened his banking app and discovered a mysterious 10-digit balance, he did what some people might do when faced with an eye-watering number: he asked ChatGPT. But for Wan Muhammad Fairus, 33, whose account should have contained less than RM1,000, his unexpected brush with billionaire status was over almost as quickly as it began. According to Berita Harian , the father of four from Samariang, Kuching, was in his bedroom preparing to make a banking transaction when he stumbled upon the extraordinary balance.

items.title: Health Ministry races to stock aerochambers and nebulisers as haze drives surge in respiratory cases
items.summary: He said the ministry had also activated the National Haze Operations Room on Sept 4 and was closely monitoring three main health conditions, namely upper respiratory tract infections (URTI), asthma and conjunctivitis, through 78 sentinel healthcare facilities. “Through the Crisis Preparedness and Response Centre (CPRC), the ministry is stepping up public health measures in response to rising Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and deteriorating air quality caused by open burning,” he said when replying to a question from Cha Kee Chin (PH-Rasah). Dzulkefly said monitoring at 78 sentinel healthcare facilities nationwide showed that URTI cases surged by 167.21 per cent to 7,065 in epidemiological week 36, compared with 2,644 cases the previous week, due to deteriorating air quality.

items.title: Teenagers among 14 charged in Gurun murder, victim allegedly tortured before body found near golf club
items.summary: The accused are Muhammad Asyraaf Muhammad Zaidi, 20; Muhammad Azrul Rahimi Muhamad Yusri, 18; Ahmad Izzul Irfan Ridduan, 21; Muhammad Rhahimy Abdul Rashid, 19; Yusman Hakimi Yusmezal, 24; Muhammad Zulfaqar Zulkarnain Khairol Fais, 21; and Muhammad Aiman Riduwan Abdullah, 21. The other accused are Ahmad Aiman Danial Ahmad Wizam, 21; Muhammad Adam Haris Rosdan, 21; Muhammad Muqkriz Azizan, 21; Muhammad Adam Iqbal Mohd Wazir, 19; Syafiq Afif Syarafuddin Abd Ghapar, 23; and two teenagers aged 16 and 17. Only three of the accused, Muhammad Azrul Rahimi, Ahmad Izzul Irfan and Muhammad Zulfaqar Zulkarnain, were represented by lawyer Mohamad Ashraf Ahmad Sohaimi.

items.title: Prisons Department probes Kajang jail after NGO flags water shortages, dirty food trays and poor hygiene
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Prisons Department is investigating allegations by a non-governmental organisation (NGO) concerning water supply disruptions, sanitation facilities and food provision at Kajang Prison. The department said it consistently prioritised inmates’ welfare, health, hygiene and safety, including the provision of basic necessities, in accordance with existing regulations and procedures. Earlier today, Lawyers for Liberty, in a statement, raised concerns over alleged water shortages and unsanitary conditions at Kajang Prison.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng urges Malaysia to sue Indonesia over haze if Jakarta rejects Asean firefighting task force
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged Malaysia to consider legal action against Indonesia to seek compensation for the worsening transboundary haze crisis if Jakarta refuses to cooperate with a proposed permanent Asean firefighting task force. Lim said the recurring crisis, which has forced schools to close and disrupted livelihoods, could no longer be treated as an annual inconvenience, calling for a coordinated regional response to tackle forest and land fires at their source. The call comes as Malaysia continues to grapple with deteriorating air quality caused by smoke from forest and land fires in Indonesia, with 34 of the country’s 68 air monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am today.

items.title: Apology on Threads but not in newspapers: Man faces contempt proceedings in Christy Ng defamation case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A man ordered to pay fashion entrepreneur Christy Ng and her company RM180,000 in damages over defamatory social media posts is facing contempt of court proceedings after allegedly failing to publish apologies in newspapers as directed by the High Court. The High Court in Kuala Lumpur has fixed Monday to hear a committal application filed by Ng and Christy Ng Sdn Bhd against J Vikneshvra Rau, Berita Harian reported. On September 15, the High Court granted Ng and her company permission to initiate committal proceedings against him for alleged contempt of court.

items.title: Fatal crash drivers could face asset seizure if compensation to victims unpaid, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Proposed amendments to federal road transport laws could empower courts to seize the assets of drivers convicted of fatal crashes if they fail to pay court-ordered compensation to victims’ families, Transport Minister Anthony Loke told Parliament today. The government is currently drafting amendments to the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333) to establish a mandatory compensation mechanism for victims and next-of-kin affected by reckless driving and driving under the influence (DUI). Replying during Question Time, Loke revealed that the ministry is exploring asset seizure alongside tougher secondary penalties, such as heavier fines or extended prison sentences to prevent convicted drivers from evading financial restitution.

items.title: Sultan Ibrahim attends day two of 273rd Conference of Rulers
items.summary: The meeting was chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah. Also in attendance were the Raja of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Jamalullail; Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah; Sultan of Kedah, Al-Aminul Karim Sultan Sallehuddin Sultan Badlishah; and Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah. Also present were the Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail; Crown Prince of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra; and Tunku Temenggong of Johor, Tunku Idris Iskandar Sultan Ibrahim.
